reviews.title: Genuine Review
reviews.text:
I've played since May 8th, roughly Day 9 or 10 of release, and it's been amazing every step of the way. I personally love every design, I love every character, and I adore the world, especially Duskmoor. Exe has just been announced as a playable character, so I've decided to write a review. Obviously, I'm a little biased since Exe has held a soft spot in my favorite design chart since I saw him in the pre-release YouTube Short, but being completely honest, the announcement that he'll be playable made me really happy. I've been saving for a while now, so fingers crossed I can get him!

Anyways, overall, on my iPhone 14, graphics are pretty smooth. Logging in is a little chunky at first, but once it settles into your device, it runs smoothly! I also love the new system they put in place with the 3 new free outfits; 1 for Baicang, 1 for Sakiri, and 1 for Haniel; and I love the vehicle designs, specifically the Porsche Spyder 918.

Overall, it's a 4.75/5 or 9.5/10, and I take half of a point off because of how difficult it is to get Fons when there's so much to spend on. But overall, great game, super F2P if you're not after outfits and stuff, and there's no 50/50, which is super appealing.

Over Zenless Zone Zero, Wuthering Waves, Honkai: Star Rail, and even Genshin, NTE has become my top comfort game. Good job, devs. I intend to become a long time player.

reviews.title: PC only, don’t bother
reviews.text: The game is made by talentless hacks who do not test on anything other than PC. All they do is try to copy every idea from every popular game in the universe, without the least bit of understanding what makes those games fun. The combat system is a shambles, where you spend most battles with the camera behind walls or other objects, having your skills that you can’t aim fling you off the tops of buildings, dodging attacks long after the attack animation completes, trying to activate character skills that appear available but are actually still on cool-down, or simply stop working until you restart. Special events are poorly conceived, and either incredibly boring (like the jet ski salvage event) or are impossible to complete on mobile/console (like the volley ball game). They seem to put a lot of effort into half-baked and then abandoned ideas that they ship anyway, so you waste a lot of time trying to figure out what to do with something that was never actually completed. The basic UX design is trash, and the UI for many screens used to manage your character are extremely broken on mobile. E.g., they clearly expect you to use a mouse wheel to scroll through lists. Using touch, you cannot swipe up/down on the list, because that starts a drag-and-drop gesture. You have to find the hidden border between items and swipe that, or try to swipe the 4-pixel wide scroll bar. Using the controller stick to cursor through items causes an item not under your cursor to be selected, often causing items you cannot see on the screen to be consumed accidentally. Every new release breaks previously working features, and the support team is useless. They’re clearly paid by how fast they close tickets. E.g., if you file a 100% reproducible crash bug with step-by-step instructions, and check the box to upload the logs, they’ll close the ticket, saying “you need to upload logs” and give instructions that only work for PC. For other bugs, if you attach a screenshot, they’ll ask for a video, then close the ticket. If you attach a video, they close the ticket and say “try restarting your PC” or “try a different controller” and to file a new bug if the bug persists. At this point, I’d have to file and re-file 10-15 bugs per day. On the plus side, since they are so lazy and incompetent, any bug that works in your favor can be exploited forever. Like Hathor’s skill to auto-complete delivery tasks, which will sometimes cost 0 energy or will refund you energy, and give you up to 12x times the reward you’re supposed to get. Well, as long as it doesn’t cause the game to freeze.

reviews.title: In game currency sucks
reviews.text: I’ve played ever since launch. This game was awesome, in terms of a fair gacha, an open world, and an interesting story. There are also tons of minigames to play, and each update is always something different. each character is unique in their own way, too. However, there are these mystery box gacha that demand a ton of fons, the in game currency in question. To earn fons, u need to complete jobs, but there is a weekly cap, for f2p and p2w. No matter what, it’s impossible to generate such a great revenue of fons in this game. And this would be fine if it wasn’t for the fact that these mystery box gachas demand a ridiculous amount of fons that are almost impossible to reach, and at the same time, usually require u to spend ur entire life savings on game to unlock the rewards u want or the exclusive reward. This also deters u from using fons to buy anything else, such as other cars or houses. So ur always forced to save up ur fons for each new mystery box gacha to unlock an exclusive reward or a skin u want, and at the same time, impossible to use fons for anything else fearing u can’t unlock what’s in the next update. And like I said, it doesn’t matter if ur f2p or p2w, it’s impossible to make enough fons for their mystery box gacha due to the stupid weekly limits that already require a long grind. NTE was good in terms of its content and story, but its in game currency is such a stupid system, these stupid fons.

reviews.title: Anomalies Everywhere
reviews.text:
Revolving around the pliable concept of “paranormal things embedded in everyday life”, NTE always finds ways to be fun and entertaining. The game never takes itself too seriously, the writing is clever, and the gacha system is generous. For a gacha.

The Mac support is very good and native, but if you’re on M2 or older, you can’t really leverage ray tracing due to a lack of hardware support.

The environment is carefully designed and reasonably interactive, but it’s also clear that it’s a lower-budget gacha at the beginning of its trajectory. The loot and character building systems lack depth.

With this creative crew, I expect the game to continue to improve, but you can already rob a bank, jet-ski, defeat anomalies, and fish with explosives on any given Sunday.

reviews.title: Early Days but Not Enough
reviews.text:
I know the game isn’t that old and just got a major update and all but it just isn’t fun. The combat is either blindly mashing buttons or failing to time a perfect dodge/parry you knew you hit.

The gacha system looks to be more generous than other titles in the genre, but with so few characters it is easy to get plenty of extra lower rank characters and starve for more of the higher tier. It is still all a push to open the wallet.

The game’s presentation is also a bit wonky. The tone is too far to either side. Is this a slice of life with goofy comedic characters or is it a ghost busting group with an eclectic cast? Humor is fine but when more than 70% of the cutscenes feel tonally deaf it is time for serious concern. Maybe I’m just getting older but the combat doesn’t hold up for me and the story and presentation are massive letdowns.

Would not recommend.

reviews.title: Close to greatness, but still far from it
reviews.text:
Pros: Gacha system is very player friendly. The way they handle character copies is unlike anything I’ve seen, and frankly, I wish it was the industry standard. The world is full of life, and every corner is interesting to explore. The art direction is just *chefs kiss*. The music and sound design is also great. Optimization is so amazing, that any negatives do not hit as hard. I cannot believe I only needed 20-25 gb to be able to play this game, games that offer the same hit upwards of 100+ gigs on a phone - an insane ask in my opinion. Seriously, you couldn’t stop me gushing about the optimization even if you tried, absolutely AMAZING work done by the dev team here. 

Cons: In lieu of a weapon banner like in other gachas, it seems like your disc drive/artifact/etc. is tied to another paid-for gacha - I’m not a fan if that’s the case. It suffers from the same issue a lot of open world games face (imo) in that they do not offer better traversal methods. Climbing feels jank, driving feels clunky (how do Roblox experiences offer better collision and turning than a game like this?), and running/jumping/walking is the same as it is anywhere else. Character designs are all over the place, the current banner character (and most everyone I’ve met so far in my 2 hours playing) looks better suited for a fantasy rpg in a magical world, not a city. It really hurts the identity of the game, and makes me see the characters as just another faceless handsome/pretty anime character. The gacha animation is interesting to say the least, but takes a little too much time and doesn’t seem to have a good alternative animation. I wouldn’t remove it, but I’d offer something more akin to the standard, a single animation letting you know if you won big or didn’t. That otter bot thing with the television for a head you meet in the first chapter is… god I actually hate that thing. 

Overall, it’s a little rough around the edges, but I’d go so far to say that it’s one of, if not the best I’ve played out of the major open world gachas. It could beat everyone out of the water if they focused a bit more on wowing their players the moment they stepped into the game. It feels too disjointed for me to take it 100% seriously. I’ve still got a lot to see and do in the game however, and I’m already much more optimistic to do so than I was in some of the other major open world gachas. Definitely a game I’m going to keep playing for a while.
